[docs/resource-guides/cloudflare/cache.md#workers-kv-type-cache]
Workers KV is Cloudflare's global key-value store: fast reads, eventually consistent writes (changes can take up to a minute to show everywhere). Use it for caches, feature flags and configuration. pskit never creates it: declare it with `external: true` and bind it. Redis clients don't work in Python Workers (no TCP sockets, no third-party packages). For Redis use an HTTP-based Redis service and call it with `from js import fetch`, or deploy that function elsewhere.

[docs/resource-guides/cloudflare/custom.md#other-cloudflare-services-and-apis-type-custom]
`custom` covers anything else a Worker talks to: a secret, Workers AI, Vectorize, another Worker, or any HTTP API. pskit only passes `connection` values to handlers (`external: true` is required). Either bind the service through `functions.<fn>.options.bindings` or call its HTTP API. Python Workers can't install packages, so use bindings or `from js import fetch` rather than SDKs.

[docs/resource-guides/cloudflare/database.md#cloudflare-databases-type-database]
From a Python Worker, use **D1** (Cloudflare's SQLite database) through a binding. PostgreSQL / MySQL drivers need TCP sockets and native code that Pyodide doesn't provide, so a Python Worker can't connect to them directly; see [PostgreSQL with Hyperdrive](#postgresql-with-hyperdrive-nodejs). `database` resources are always `external: true`: pskit only passes their details along.
